interest: Documents the policy transition from complete Japanese demilitarization to early Cold War debates and allied anxieties over rearmament.
keywords: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
overview: This file comprises State and War Department records from April 1945 through December 1949 detailing U.S. and Allied policies regarding the Japanese military during the close of World War II and the postwar occupation. Beginning with wartime intelligence on Japanese army commands and prisoner-of-war interrogations on morale and imperial loyalty, the records document the implementation of total demilitarization, demobilization, and destruction of military equipment under directives from the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers (SCAP) and the Far Eastern Commission. The collection culminates in late-1949 high-level State Department policy analyses and diplomatic despatches debating whether to reactivate Japanese armed forces or retain U.S. bases in connection with the Japanese peace treaty, alongside reports of international anxieties from Pacific allies regarding potential remilitarization.
